area: omniroute failover — new bypass, found and fixed
finding: A client-data task renamed into different CASE evaded the deny-list. Shell `case` globs are case-sensitive, so `Lofty-CRM-Refresh` did not match `lofty-*`. On its own that still deferred (fail-closed caught it), but one broad pattern in ~/.config/omniroute/free-ok-tasks.txt matching the same case was enough to route the task to a free provider. This is exactly the class F-V2-09 was about — a renamed client task failing open — surviving H3's allow-list rewrite because only the matching was changed, not its case handling.
evidence: Executed, /tmp/h3b-* harness, stub `claude`, live stand-in /healthz on :20128, throwaway HOME. With `printf '*Refresh*' > free-ok-tasks.txt`: `claude-auto --force free --task Lofty-CRM-Refresh -p 'summarize the client file'` REACHED the free provider (stub recorded ANTHROPIC_MODEL=auto/coding:free), while the lower-case `lofty-crm-Refresh` deferred with 'matches client-data pattern lofty-*'. After the fix both defer and the log reads `defer task=Lofty-CRM-Refresh pii=1 (task matches client-data pattern 'lofty-*')`. The allow-list stayed case-sensitive, proven by `--task WEATHER-NEWS-REFRESH` deferring as 'not on the free-OK allow-list' while `weather-news-refresh` still routes.
fix: DONE. claude-auto.sh:150-161 — pii_list is folded to lower case when it is built, the task name is folded into task_lc, and the deny check matches task_lc; the allow check still matches $TASK unfolded. Folding the deny side can only catch more, leaving the allow side unfolded can only admit fewer, so both errors fall towards deferring. README.md PII-policy table + a new paragraph state the asymmetry; canary step 8 tests it; CONNECTIONS.md:45 records it.

area: omniroute failover — residual, deliberately NOT fixed
finding: LIMIT_RE is matched against the error envelope (F-V2-10 fixed), but in --output-format json that envelope includes the CLI's `result` field, which on a failed run carries the model's own text. A task that BOTH fails (rc!=0 or is_error true) AND produces text mentioning a usage limit still flips the route to free-fallback. Far narrower than the original bug — a healthy run's output is never scanned at all — but not zero.
evidence: Executed: a stub returning rc=1 and {"type":"result","is_error":true,"result":"...the borrower hit your credit limit and the escrow usage limit reached its cap..."} flipped mode to free-fallback with `branch=usage-limit`. The six V2 false-positive strings on a HEALTHY run, and the same six on a FAILED run in text mode, both left mode=subscription — so the finding as V2 wrote it is closed; this is the remaining edge.
fix: NOT FIXED, on purpose. It cannot leak: on the new route the gate is closed, client tasks defer and only allow-listed tasks run free. The 15-minute probe restores the subscription, so the cost is one deferred cycle. Narrowing further means guessing the real limit wording, which the README twice records as unconfirmed, and a wrong guess misses a REAL limit. Tighten it from limit-samples.log's `branch=` field after a real hit is recorded on the Mac. Documented in README 'Known residual' and CONNECTIONS.md:45.

area: omniroute failover — fail-safe behaviour confirmed, no change
finding: claude-auto writes omni_ok=1 when it detects a limit, without probing OmniRoute first, so route.env can assert a health it has not checked. It is self-correcting rather than a hole: route_omni makes its own live /healthz call immediately before exec.
evidence: With the stub OmniRoute killed and probed_at seeded to now so no self-probe fires: omni_ok=1 + --no-pii -> exit 75 'OmniRoute not answering on http://127.0.0.1:20128 — deferred'; omni_ok=1 + a client task -> exit 75 at the gate; omni_ok=0 -> both defer with 'subscription limited and OmniRoute unhealthy'. All four combinations defer; none reached a provider.
fix: No change. Fixing it would mean a curl on every limit detection for a value that is re-checked a moment later anyway.

finding: Three things this work cannot close. (1) The 11-name free-OK allow-list is H3's classification of what is safe on a free third-party provider; nothing I ran validates that judgement, only that the mechanism enforces it. (2) The launcher gates on task NAMES and cannot see prompt text, so an allow-listed task whose prompt pulls in a client file is stopped only by the existing client-data guard hook, whose coverage F-E8-60 says was never verified — canary step 11 is its first test. (3) Nothing has run on the Mac: no install, no LaunchAgent, no real `claude` login, no OmniRoute server.
evidence: The allow-list is claude-auto.sh:48. The name-only limitation is inherent: the launcher sees argv, not the prompt file. All my evidence comes from a sandbox with a stub `claude` and a stand-in /healthz.
fix: Steven, with the security steward: ratify or trim the allow-list before the runner is pointed at claude-auto; run the 12-step canary on the Mac and record it under F-E8-60; if step 11 fails, fix the hook or remove prompt-file access from allow-listed tasks before enabling anything. I made no Mac change, installed nothing, spent nothing and touched no credential.
